value.title: dd standalone extraction — CLI + SDK port out of harness-engineering
value.summary: Port the dd subsystem (45 SDK files + 13 CLI acts, ~10.6k LOC, ~51 tests) out of harness-engineering into @ai-substrate/dd as a dual-surface CLI + typed SDK, packable standalone; handover = SDK passable to koala.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: dd (deterministic documents) ships today inside harness-engineering as the harness dd verb family. This plan extracts it into this repo as @ai-substrate/dd: the near-self-contained SDK core (services/dd, 45 files, one external import) ports near-verbatim; the 13 CLI acts re-land on this repo stub envelope seam; the package gains subpath exports covering the measured consumer surface (dossier F-04) and must pack standalone (npm proxy lag makes the tarball the consume path). Final phase self-hosts: this repo works its own documents with the ported dd bin, and the SDK is handed to pij-related-koala, who integrates it into harness and strips the old in-tree code (explicitly not this plan). A PM runs implementation; phases are grouped logically by cohesive subsystem, not by sequencing.

sections.name: goals
value: SDK core ports near-verbatim: all 45 services/dd files under src/, importing only node: builtins + a local posix-path shim
All 10 planned verbs (validate schema docs build address link links graph doctor write) registered and working — dd status reports ok, exit 0
Plumbing parity with upstream acts: adapters env/exec/fs/hash/process/loader + output/style added to the stub seam; jiti joins commander as the only runtime deps
Subpath exports mirror the subdirectory structure and cover the measured consumer surface (dossier F-04) — koala can express every harness import against this package
~51 upstream tests + 4 fixture dirs ported and green under just checks; the ~9 consumer tests stay upstream
--json works postfix on every verb (dd status --json) and the AGENTS.md example is fixed
npm pack from a clean clone yields a tarball that installs and runs standalone — a checked gate, not an assumption
Self-hosting: this repo works its own dd documents with the local bin (harness plan validate excepted)
dd-next backlog (17 items) migrated with status/ownership annotations and the #8-11 ordering constraint intact
Handover packet to pij-related-koala: tarball + exports map + surface notes — the definition of done

sections.name: non_goals
value: Harness-side integration and stripping the old in-tree dd (koala's task, explicitly not this plan)
npm publish, tags, GitHub releases, or release enablement (Jordan's)
Resolving OPEN backlog items (#8, #13 and the vocabulary cluster #8-12) — they migrate annotated, unresolved
Changing dd behaviour beyond the postfix --json fix and packaging seams — this is a port, not a rewrite
Any write, build, or install inside the harness-engineering checkout
PR ceremony — work lands on main per Jordan 2026-08-07; CI green is the bar

value.claim: SDK standalone: every services/dd file lives under src/ with imports resolving to node: builtins or the local posix-path shim only — proven by tsc clean build + a grep gate that fails on any other external import path in the SDK tree

Consumer surface importable: for EVERY import specifier observed in harness consumers (dossier F-04): core/address (parseAddress, isAddressFailure), core/model (DdDoc), core/parse (parse), core/validate (DdIssue, collectLinkCells), core/walk (validateWalk), links barrel (MemoizingDocLoader, resolveMapSeed, traverseCorpus), schema/model (SchemaIssue), schema/resolve AND schema/index (ConventionSchemaResolver via both), render/renderer (escapeCell, headingSlug) — a test imports one named symbol from each EXACT subpath and the exports map carries those exact paths (explicit or wildcard). The plan barrel (buildPlanIndex, itemKey, PlanEdge/PlanIndex/PlanItem) is EXCLUDED from the public map until OQ-2 is ruled (phase 3); until then it is proven importable internally only.
Port ledger green: dd status exits 0 with ported[10] / remaining[0], and each verb registered only in the commit that made it actually work (ledger honesty preserved through history)
Envelope contract: every ported verb exits through exitWithEnvelope; exit map 0 ok/degraded, 2 unconfigured, 1 error holds — existing envelope tests extended to cover every ported verb
--json accepted postfix on every verb (dd status --json exits per its status, not E002) AND program-level prefix still works; AGENTS.md example corrected
Test parity: the audited port set (~51 of 60, classified by import direction before any move) runs green under just checks; zero flow-dd consumer tests ported; the audit table is committed

Pack gate: npm pack from a clean clone installs into a temp project (registry/proxy access permitted for the DECLARED runtime deps commander+jiti; the dd source repo absent from every resolution path) and dd validate + dd build run against a fixture corpus including a jiti-loaded custom type. npm pack --dry-run file list proves the tarball carries bin+dist+LICENSE and no repo-external requires survive in dist.
Self-hosting: dd build --check reports zero drift over docs/plans/001-dd-extraction using the LOCAL bin; harness plan validate (harness-side) still green over the same corpus
Backlog migrated: all 17 dd-next items in this repo tracker with status/ownership annotations and the #8-before-#11 ordering constraint stated; OPEN items still open
Docs shipped: README standalone quick-start + docs/how carrying the two baked entries; CI green on main at completion

value.title: SDK core port
value.brief: Copy services/dd (45 files, 7 subdirs) into src/ near-verbatim with a local posix-path shim; port the SDK-side test corpus (~40 files) + its 4 fixture dirs into test/; FIRST read the two upstream architecture tests (dd-core-isolation, dd-plan-semantics-frozen) and port the isolation ratchet as this repo guard; commit the import-direction audit of all 60 tests; record the upstream basis SHA; sketch the subpath-exports skeleton. Logical group: THE SDK — everything that is dd-the-library.

value.title: CLI acts + plumbing parity
value.brief: Bring the stub to plumbing parity (output/style.ts + adapters env/exec/fs/hash/process/loader; add jiti dep), then land all 13 acts on the envelope seam and register the ten verbs — dd status flips green verb-by-verb, honestly. Fix --json to postfix-tolerant and correct AGENTS.md. Extend envelope tests over every ported verb. Logical group: THE CLI — everything that is dd-the-binary.

value.title: Package & release readiness
value.brief: Freeze the exports map against the F-04 consumer surface (OQ-1/OQ-2 must be ruled by here — workshop open), wire prepack build, and prove the tarball gate: npm pack from clean clone -> temp install -> validate+build incl. a jiti-loaded custom type. README quick-start + docs/how ported entries. Logical group: THE PACKAGE — everything between working code and a consumable artifact.

value.title: Self-hosting + handover
value.brief: Switch this repo document work to the LOCAL dd bin (harness plan validate stays harness-side); dd build --check clean over this plan folder; migrate the 17-item dd-next backlog with annotations + ordering constraint; assemble the handover packet for pij-related-koala (tarball + exports map + surface notes + basis SHA); CI green on main. Logical group: SELF-HOSTING + HANDOVER — proof by consumption.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: 📚 Incorporates findings from assets/research-dossier.md (2026-08-07, Standard effort, F-01..F-10, H-01..H-03, 5 risks). Headlines: services/dd imports exactly ONE external file (posix-path) so the SDK ports near-verbatim; all harness coupling sits in the 13 acts; runtime deps land at commander + jiti; ~51 of 60 tests port, ~9 stay upstream as the consume-step proof; two architecture tests (dd-core-isolation, dd-plan-semantics-frozen) may already encode the extraction boundary.

value.approach: Hybrid — the ~51 ported upstream tests are the spine of proof and must pass unmodified where possible; new seams (plumbing shims, postfix --json, pack gate, exports map) get targeted new tests, TDD only where behaviour is new.
value.rationale: The port inherits a mature corpus for free; re-labelling it TDD adds ceremony without proof. New standalone-only behaviour (packaging, exports) has no upstream tests and earns them.
value.focus_areas: ported-test parity; envelope/exit contract on every ported verb; tarball-installs-standalone incl. a jiti custom-type load; consumer-surface import test (one F-04 symbol per subpath)
value.excluded: re-testing upstream-proven dd semantics beyond the ported corpus; consumer (flow-dd-*) tests, which stay harness-side
value.mock_usage: Real fixtures only — 4 fixture dirs port with the tests; dd is a filesystem tool, real files are cheap and honest (matches upstream).

value.location: Hybrid — README.md gains standalone install/quick-start (npm front door); docs/how/ receives the ported dd concept docs (dd-overview, how-to-add-a-schema) plus a note on the .dd resolution ladder.
value.rationale: An npm-published package needs a README; the baked docs already exist and port with the docs verb — open question on verbatim vs rewrite.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: Standing assumptions: harness-engineering checkout is READ-ONLY reference (never build/write there); no npm publish or provenance experiments; release workflows stay inert until Jordan enables them; the npm proxy runs ~1wk behind registry so the tarball is the consume path; Jordan authorized landing on main with CI green as the end state (2026-08-07 pipeline ruling — supersedes the earlier no-push posture for this repo only). Assumption: upstream dd source at harness-engineering main is the port basis; if koala lands dd changes upstream mid-port, the PM rebases the affected phase before review.

value.question: OQ-1 (Jordan): SDK-as-library vs CLI-shelled consumption for harness — Jordan leaned CLI-first, but acts/plan consumes dd as a library today (F-04). Decides how much surface is public API under semver. Must resolve before phase 3 exports freeze.

OQ-2 (Jordan): does services/dd/plan (consumed by harness plan validate, guarded upstream by dd-plan-semantics-frozen) ship in the public SDK surface, stay internal, or stay harness-side? Not a clean either/or — part of the semantics is dd-side already.
OQ-3: do the two baked doc entries (dd-overview, how-to-add-a-schema) port verbatim or get rewritten for standalone context? Default verbatim; rewrite only on Jordan ask.

value.why: OQ-1/OQ-2 both land here: which subpaths are public, whether plan/ ships, and what semver promises attach. Cheap to workshop before phase 3; expensive to re-cut after koala consumes.
value.key_questions: Which of the 7 subdirs are public subpaths? Is plan/ exported? What does the tarball export map literally contain?

value.question: Workflow mode?
value.answer: Full — multi-phase, PM-run, all gates (CS-4 scale).

value.question: Testing strategy?
value.answer: Hybrid — ported upstream tests are the spine; targeted new tests for new seams only.

value.question: Mock usage?
value.answer: Real fixtures only — matches upstream dd practice.

value.question: Documentation?
value.answer: Hybrid — README quick-start + docs/how ported concept docs.

value.question: Phase design principle?
value.answer: Jordan: group phases LOGICALLY by cohesive subsystem, never by sequencing; a PM implements.

value.question: Operating model?
value.answer: Jordan: prime authors phase-N tasks -> PM implements (coder claude-opus-5 xhigh, reviewer gpt-5.6-terra high, /builder skill) -> at PM going-to-review the prime prepares phase N+1 tasks (pipelined) -> autonomous to completion. End state CI green on main, no PR. Questions to Jordan via pij telegram.

value.question: Tooling posture?
value.answer: Jordan: plan authored dd-native (this document); late-stage the repo self-hosts on its own ported dd bin, except harness plan validate which stays harness-side. Handover = SDK passable to koala; koala integrates + strips upstream (not this plan).

sections.name: implementation_summary
sections.value: Four logically-grouped phases (Jordan: group by cohesive subsystem, never by sequencing), each a PM-run unit with its own task file: (1) SDK core — copy services/dd verbatim + posix-path shim + its ~40 unit tests + fixtures, subpath exports skeleton; (2) CLI acts + plumbing — the missing adapters/output pieces, jiti dep, all 13 acts on the stub envelope seam, postfix --json fix, acts tests; (3) Package & release readiness — exports map frozen against the F-04 surface, prepack build, the tarball-installs-standalone gate incl. jiti custom-type load, README + docs/how; (4) Self-hosting + handover — this repo works its own documents with the local dd bin (harness plan validate stays harness-side), backlog migrated with annotations intact, handover packet to koala. The dd status ledger is the running honesty gate: it flips green only when all ten verbs actually register.

value.finding: services/dd imports exactly ONE file outside its tree (services/shared/posix-path.js) — the SDK is near-self-contained (dossier F-01).
value.action: Phase 1 is copy + one shim, not a de-tangling effort; any new external import the port introduces is a defect.

value.finding: src/app.ts verb registry is the single convergence point — all ten verbs register in one file (dossier: sequencing watch).
value.action: PM serializes registry merges; with one coder per phase this is a hot-spot to watch, not a blocker.

value.finding: All harness coupling lives in the 13 acts: output×5 + adapters×7 + commander (F-02); the stub already mirrors envelope/error-codes/exit/output-port/clock (F-03).
value.action: Phase 2 adds only style.ts + adapters env/exec/fs/hash/process/loader — a bounded, enumerable gap list.

value.finding: Runtime deps land at exactly commander + jiti 2.7.0 (custom-type adapter loading in build/doctor/validate/shared); picomatch is NOT used by dd (F-06).
value.action: Add jiti; the pack gate must exercise a jiti-loading path or a broken dep ships silently.

value.finding: Two architecture tests upstream (dd-core-isolation, dd-plan-semantics-frozen) likely encode the extraction boundary (F-10) — unopened at plan time.
value.action: Phase 1 first task: read both and port the isolation ratchet as this repo own guard; surface any boundary conflict to the prime before proceeding.

value.finding: ~9 of 60 tests are harness-consumer tests (flow-dd-*, builder-dd-teaching, dd-flow-gate int) that import flow internals not present here (F-07).
value.action: Tasks-time audit classifies all 60 by import direction BEFORE any move; the audit table commits with phase 1.

value.finding: The .dd resolution ladder (gitroot/.dd -> .harness/.dd -> ~/.dd) is dd-owned and portable (F-05); this repo now carries the builder schema family copied verbatim.
value.action: Port the ladder untouched; schema exemplar VALUES stay verbatim (dd-next #8-11 ordering — wrong Partial propagates by imitation).

value.finding: The stub --json is program-level and position-sensitive: dd status --json exits 1 E002 while dd --json status works; AGENTS.md documents the failing form (F-08).
value.action: Fix to postfix-tolerant in phase 2 while porting acts; fix the AGENTS.md example in the same commit.

value.mitigation: Open question OQ-1 priced and put to Jordan BEFORE phase 3 freezes exports; the F-04 surface is the floor either way.

value.risk: Working on main with pipelined phases: a red phase blocks the next phase landing (no branch isolation).
value.mitigation: Each phase lands only when just checks is green locally; CI on push is the backstop; review cycle completes before the next phase merges its registry edits.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: harness-engineering checkout is READ-ONLY reference — never write, build, or install there; the port basis SHA is recorded in phase 1 and rebased deliberately, never silently.
No npm publish, no --provenance, no tags, no releases — Jordan publishes. Landing on main + CI green IS authorized (Jordan 2026-08-07); conventional commits are load-bearing for release-please.
.the-flow-state.json / the-flow.json / the-flow.md are builder-owned — no hand writes, either repo.
src/app.ts registry is the convergence hot-spot: one phase in flight at a time lands registry edits; the PM serializes if pipelined phases both touch it.
.dd/schemas exemplar VALUES stay verbatim (dd-next #8-11: running the generator first turns the gate green over undetermined values — do not resolve the vocabulary as a side effect).
Every phase ends just checks green locally before handing to review; the dd status ledger must never claim a verb that does not work.

RENDERER AUTHORITY SPLIT (o-prime 2026-08-07, from the tk-0003 banner collision): from the tk-0003 landing commit onward, THIS repo documents are mutated/rendered ONLY by the LOCAL dd bin (set/add/rm/build) — upstream harness dd set/build on them is forbidden (its renderer silently regresses the banner). harness plan validate REMAINS the semantic authority (checks/gates/contradictions, per Jordan: plan checks stay harness-side); drift authority is LOCAL dd build --check. A harness-reported drift is adjudicated: local check green + banner-only diff = renderer skew (expected until koala swaps upstream), anything else = real. Window closes at handover.

OUT-OF-DIFF ASSERTION SWEEP (o-prime 2026-08-07, after TWO out-of-diff escapes: the write-family ledger gap and the CI package-smoke latent red): every review packet includes a repo-wide sweep for assertions about the changed behaviour living OUTSIDE the diff — CI configs, docs, ledgers, baked strings. Diff-scoped review is structurally blind there; the sweep is the reviewer floor, not a per-packet habit.

CORRECTION to the renderer-authority guardrail (measured by the PM): harness plan validate is NOT drift-affected — drift comparison is build alone. Blast radius of the banner skew = upstream write path + upstream dd build --check (E422 false-fail). The authority split stands; the harness-drift adjudication clause in the earlier row describes a case that cannot occur and is superseded here (append-only, prior row retained).

MEASURED-AT STAMPING (o-prime 2026-08-07; sharpened by the PM after the o-prime applied it to its own record). Any count or completeness claim in an execution-log entry, receipt, report, commit message, brief or flow comment carries the commit SHA it was measured at PLUS the re-derivation command. A claim without its SHA is an assertion, not a measurement, and re-rots silently as the repo moves. THE RULE BINDS AT THE MOMENT OF MAKING SOMETHING AUTHORITATIVE, not merely at the moment of counting: a loose wrong number costs nothing until someone puts it in a durable artifact, and whoever does that owns the defect regardless of who first said it. Instances: CI assertion, write-family ledger, sibling-count receipt, and the o-prime's own stale first-push premise. TENSE IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, NOT THE VALUE (o-prime + PM, after sweeping the orient-local defect for propagation and finding none). Three kinds of claim, and only one decays: a CONTRACT claim asserts a rule and never rots; a PAST-TENSE record stamped to a commit is correct forever, because it describes what was measured then; a PRESENT-TENSE state claim in a document meant to stay current has no expiry and no owner, and every instance of this class has had that shape. PROTECTIVE COROLLARY: never sweep stamped history. An auditor who 'fixes' phase-2's execution log for saying ported[validate,schema,docs] exit 2 would DESTROY EVIDENCE while believing they were removing rot — that entry is a correct historical record, and the stamp is precisely what makes it legible as history rather than as a stale current claim. Assert contracts, stamp states, and DERIVE anything that must read as current. THE STAMP CAN BE PERFORMED AS THEATRE (PM + reviewer, phase-4 review, the sharpest critique of this rule so far). The handover packet stated the push as 46 commits WITH THE RE-DERIVATION COMMAND PRINTED BENEATH IT — and that command does not produce 46: it gives 57 at the packet's own declared base, 58 at the review SHA, 59 on the next run. The figure was already stale at its own stamp. Printing a command beside a number does not make the number derived; the command was RECORDED, NOT RUN, so measured-at was satisfied in form and violated in substance. A stamp is evidence only if someone ran the thing at the moment they wrote it. For a fast-decaying value — a commit count, a branch delta, anything that moves every commit — even an honestly-run stamp is wrong by the time a reader arrives, so DO NOT STATE IT AT ALL: print the command and let it be the answer.

TYPECHECK IS NOT IMPLIED BY GREEN TESTS (PM-measured during the phase-3 fix round; fixed at c0af550): vitest STRIPS types, so a test file can be fully green while the test lane does not typecheck. 'The tests pass' is therefore NOT sufficient proof for a test-lane change — only just checks is. Binding on every remaining phase (all of them add tests) and on every reviewer accepting a test-lane diff.

CLAIM-OUTRAN-IMPLEMENTATION is the unifying defect class (named by the phase-3 coder, endorsed by the PM and o-prime 2026-08-07). The vacuous README guard, the stale CI package-smoke assertion, and the over-confident sibling-count receipt are ONE failure: a test or receipt whose CLAIM outran its IMPLEMENTATION, surviving review because the claim was read instead of the code. The coder's line is the rule: A GUARD'S DOCSTRING IS A HYPOTHESIS UNTIL A MUTATION REDS IT. Guardrails 7 (out-of-diff sweep), 9 (measured-at stamping) and this one are three instruments against the same class — cite this row when explaining why any of them exists.

AUTHORITY IS A SHA, NEVER A WORKING TREE (o-prime 2026-08-07, from a near-miss the PM caught). A ruling, brief, guardrail or constraint is actionable only as COMMITTED text that can be cited by SHA. Working-tree text is never authority, and a governance file read mid-write is actively dangerous: the coder read this plan's ESC-1 ruling out of the-flow.json while it was still being repaired, and the text it saw had two branch names missing to a shell-substitution defect. It refused to act and escalated, which is the second line of defence; NOT OPENING the file was the first, since flow files are a forbidden path in every packet. Two individually-survivable faults (a transcription loss and a read-mid-write) compound into a wrong implementation. Corollaries: verbatim-critical text travels as a file plus pointer, never as an argv string; and a ruling that arrives by any channel other than the recipient's own chain of command is not actionable, whatever it says.

DERIVE THE COMMIT MESSAGE, DO NOT COMPOSE IT (plan 001 P-1, raised by the PM after the o-prime's third instance). Write the commit message body from `git diff --cached`, not from what you intended to stage. The o-prime produced this class three times — a task title claiming a freeze that was held, a stale first-push premise, and a message that omitted 212 lines of another agent's work it actually carried. All three are the same shape as the stamped-but-unrun figure: RECORDED, NOT RUN. Filed as its own row rather than a clause of the measured-at rule because the ACTION differs — that rule says stamp or derive a measurement; this one says read what you are about to commit before you describe it.

A DECAYING FIGURE CAN WEAKEN AN ARGUMENT, NOT JUST AN HONESTY CLAIM (plan 001 P-3, found by the phase-4 coder re-sweeping on the could-this-rot test after rejecting its own first pass). The handover packet's STRONGEST claim was resting on a decaying number: 'library consumption is forced' was carried by a count of type-only symbols. The claim never needed the count — the argument is structural — so it had inherited that number's decay for nothing. THE FIX IS NOT TO STAMP THE FIGURE; IT IS TO NOTICE THE ARGUMENT NEVER NEEDED IT. When a figure appears inside an argument, ask what the argument would lose without it: if nothing, cut it; stamp it only where it is genuinely load-bearing. COROLLARY: decoupling can also reveal a claim leaning on its WEAKER support — here the type-erasure argument is rebuttable ('so redeclare the types'), while the load-bearing support is that two loaders are INJECTED INTO dd's walks and two helpers are called INLINE per table cell. Ask which support is actually carrying the claim. SECOND CORRECTION: strengthening an argument is itself a place claims outrun evidence, and the direction of the error is predictable — you overshoot toward the MODAL claim (impossible, always, never) because it reads stronger. A claim about SUBSTITUTION is provable; a claim about POSSIBILITY hands your reader a technicality that discredits a correct recommendation. Prefer the form that puts a COST in front of the decision-maker over the form that puts a BARRIER there.
